title: MicroRNA in vivo delivery to human pancreas tumor xenografts on chicken eggs
protocol: Clean and disinfect the incubator.
Set the incubator temperature to 37.8°C.
Place a large water tube with approximately 2 L distilled water on the bottom of the incubator.
Ensure that the humidity inside the incubator is between 45-55% using a hygrometer.
Run the incubator for 24 hours before starting the incubation.
Place the incubator at least 50 cm from the ground.
Avoid placing the incubator near heaters or in direct sunlight.
Ensure free space around ventilation windows to facilitate proper air circulation.
Clean eggs immediately upon arrival from the hatchery using 70% and 37°C warm ethanol.
Place cleaned eggs vertically in the incubator with the pointed side downwards.
Activate the shaking mechanism.
Consider the development of the chick embryo as Embryonic Development Day (EDD) 0.
Avoid storing eggs for more than 1 day upon delivery.
Store eggs at a temperature between 8-12°C if immediate use is not possible.
Wear sterile gloves while handling the eggs to minimize infection risk.
Switch off the shaking mechanism of the incubator at EDD 4.
Wash the eggs with 37°C warm 70% ethanol and place them in a horizontal position on an egg cup.
Place a 5 cm Leukosilk® strip on the middle and round parts of the egg.
Crack a 1.5 mm hole through the Leukosilk® at the dull end over the air sack with sharp scissors.
Remove 3 mL of albumen using a syringe to detach embryonic structures from the shell.
Enlarge the hole with scissors to a diameter of approximately 1.5 cm x 2.5 cm.
Check for embryo viability by observing sharply delimited blood vessels and a beating heart.
Waste non-fertilized eggs or those containing dead embryos.
Re-inject 1-2 mL of previously removed albumen into the egg.
Cover the window with a new Leukosilk® strip.
Replace the egg in the incubator in a horizontal position without shaking.
Ensure the egg is dry and free from any traces of albumen to avoid infection.
Control humidity inside the incubator using a hygrometer regularly.
Add water inside the incubator over weekends to maintain proper humidity levels for developing eggs.
Prepare Thermanox™ coverslips by punching a hole with scissors to a diameter of 9 mm.
Store prepared coverslips in a sterile petri dish filled with 70% ethanol.
Count the total number of viable/fertilized eggs.
Divide the eggs into desired experimental groups, ensuring a minimum of 20 eggs per group.
Consider preparing 20% more eggs than required to account for potential survival issues post-transplantation.
At EDD 9, ensure sufficient tumor cells are grown for transplantation at a rate of 5×10^5 cells per egg.
Determine the optimal EDD for xenotransplantation, considering that EDD 9 is suitable for pancreatic cancer cell transplantation but earlier time points may also be appropriate based on literature.
Optionally, lipofect tumor cells in vitro with 50 nm of miR-NC and let-7c mimics two days prior to xenotransplantation.
Ensure control cells remain untreated.
Prepare master mixes on EDD9 based on cell requirements per egg: mix 5×10^5 cells in 25 µL DMEM with an equal volume of matrigel.
Take eggs out of the incubator, place them on an egg holder, and remove Leukosilk® strip.
Place perforated sterile Thermanox™ coverslips on the CAM, ensuring they surround clear blood vessels without covering the embryo.
Gently scratch the CAM inside the ring with a syringe needle to ensure immediate blood supply for the xenograft.
Pipette 50 µL cell/matrigel suspension into the rings in the scratched regions.
Tape the hole in the shell with Leukosilk® and return eggs to the incubator, avoiding shaking.
Prepare master mixes on EDD14 consisting of 50 nM miRNA-lipofectamine in chick saline for each egg.
Gently mix the miRNA-lipofectamine master mixes by pipetting up and down before injection.
Examine the blood vessels on the CAM.
Gently insert the needle at a 90° angle into the chosen vein.
Slowly dispense the treatment through the needle.
Remove the needle gently from the blood vessel.
Arrest any bleeding with sterile cotton buds.
Take eggs out of the incubator on EDD18.
Remove the Leukosilk® strip carefully.
Enlarge the window in the eggshell to approximately 4 cm in diameter.
Inject 50 µL Narcoren® into a CAM vessel from a 16 g/100 mL stock solution, or alternatively inject 25 µl Ketanest® of a 50 mg/ml esketaminhydrochlorid stock solution.
Lift the CAM area where the tumor is growing with forceps.
Resect the tumor without injuring the embryo.
Place resected tumors in a petri dish on ice.
Determine the size of the resected tumors using calipers.
Take the embryo out of the eggshell, ensuring the connection between embryo and yolk sac remains intact.
Inject 50 to 100 µL Narcoren® intraperitoneally.
ALTERNATIVELY: Inject 25 µl of a 50 mg/ml Ketanest® stock solution.
Control 10-15 min later if the heart beat of the embryo stopped; inject more Narcoren® or Ketanest® if necessary.
Resect embryonal organs like lungs, liver, and CAM.
Exclude embryos that died before EDD18 from further analyses.
Estimate tumor volumes using the formula: Volume = 4/3×Π×r³ (r =1/2×√ of diameter 1×diameter 2).
Store tissues in cryotubes on dry ice and store at -80°C.
Embed tissues in Tissue-Tek® O.C.T™ compound for future analysis.
Observe the resulting embryos for toxicity by physical examination.
Weigh and obtain the mean weight of the embryos from different experimental groups.
